headline: High: Flowise can write shared files and browse/egress while kotaemon reads local app data and sends content to external model APIs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the filesystem and run browsers, while kotaemon ingests documents and chat transcripts through a web UI. If Flowise outputs are placed into kotaemon’s document or chat inputs, malicious instructions can ride the shared file path. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation, so the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are copied into kotaemon document uploads or chat transcripts
IF both agents share a writable workspace without provenance labels
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic ingestion of Flowise-generated files into kotaemon
Add a manual review step before importing any shared artifact
Tag imported files with source and timestamp
requires-engineering: add provenance metadata checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials and has broad network egress; kotaemon handles API keys and sends content to external model APIs such as OpenAI and AzureOpenAI. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive documents, transcripts, or secrets can move from Flowise into kotaemon and then out to third-party APIs. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default configurations.
conditions: IF Flowise and kotaemon share any writable workspace or uploaded-file directory
IF kotaemon routes imported content to OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Groq, or similar APIs
mitigations: Store secrets in separate vaults per agent
Block shared filesystem access between the two services
Restrict kotaemon connectors to local-only models for shared data
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise supports multiple instances with shared state via a server datastore and can write the filesystem; kotaemon also supports multiple instances and writes ./ktem_app_data. If both operate on the same host or volume, concurrent writes can collide on shared mutable resources. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict risk is real but bounded to state corruption rather than guaranteed loss.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed on the same host or shared volume
IF Flowise server datastore and kotaemon ./ktem_app_data overlap or are bind-mounted together
mitigations: Use separate volumes for each agent
Run only one writer per shared directory
Snapshot data before concurrent maintenance
Check for file-lock support in the deployment
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can consume documents and citations. If kotaemon treats Flowise-produced content as authoritative without verification, errors or fabricated citations can cascade into downstream answers. The pairwise pathway is plausible, but the profiles do not show autonomous action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF kotaemon ingests Flowise outputs as source documents or citations
IF no human or automated verification step checks those outputs before answering
mitigations: Require source verification before indexing Flowise outputs
Mark Flowise-generated artifacts as untrusted
Compare citations against original documents
Limit Flowise outputs to drafts only
requires-engineering: add confidence and provenance scoring

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while kotaemon touches documents, transcripts, and API keys and can send content to external model providers. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through both, retention and processor boundaries can diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents or transcripts are processed by both agents
IF the deployment requires a specific residency, retention, or DPA boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flows
Document retention settings for both systems
Disable external API connectors for sensitive workloads
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
